## Highlights
Fan control now tells you when it cannot work instead of pretending it can. If the privileged helper is not installed or has not been approved, ChillMac says so and gives you a button to fix it.
This release re-registers that helper, so macOS will ask you to approve ChillMac once under Login Items & Extensions. Fan control stays unavailable until you do. Later releases go back to a single click.
## Fixed
- **The window could open completely blank.** The popover sometimes showed only its background with every card invisible, reported on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs - **The menu bar icon closes the window again.** Clicking it while the window was open closed and immediately reopened it, so it never appeared to close at all - **Fan control did nothing on Intel Macs from 2018 onward.** Those machines need a different SMC key than older Intel models, and ChillMac only ever wrote the old one. Sliders moved and reported success while the fan stayed on automatic - **Performance Mode no longer claims fans it cannot reach.** With the helper missing, the toggle, the curve percentage and the sliders all looked live. Monitoring was never affected: temperature, RPM, CPU, memory and battery readings have always been accurate - **The privileged helper now verifies who is talking to it.** It previously accepted fan commands from any process on your Mac, and now accepts them only from ChillMac - **Fans are reliably returned to automatic when you quit.** That request was sent as the app exited and usually did not arrive, leaving fans pinned at their last manual speed - **Two crashes and a hang.** One in memory reporting, one in the FPS counter, and a stall that could freeze the app while it read hardware information
## Improvements
- **Smoother sliders and lighter background work.** Setting a fan speed takes a fraction of the work it used to, dragging a slider sends a couple of commands instead of one per step, and battery and disk readings moved off the main thread

Battery health now matches the number macOS reports.
## Fixed
- **Battery health percentage.** ChillMac was calculating it from the raw gauge reading and coming out several percent low. It now reads the same value System Settings shows - **Max Capacity (mAh).** Now derived from the same measurement as the health percentage, so the two agree

## Highlights
Fan control didn't work on recent installs, and this fixes it.
ChillMac changes fan speeds through a small privileged helper that runs in the background. On any reasonably recent install, that helper was never actually getting installed — the app asked macOS to register it at every launch, the request failed, and the failure only went to the system log. Nothing in the interface said anything was wrong. Sliders moved, Performance Mode looked engaged, and no fan ever changed speed.
Monitoring was never affected — temperatures, CPU, memory, battery and fan RPM readouts were always accurate, because reading doesn't need the helper. Only changing fan speed did.
## Fixed
- **The privileged helper now installs correctly.** The app bundle was missing the launch daemon definition that macOS reads to install it, so registration failed every time with "Unable to read plist". The definition is now built into the app, and the helper registers, starts on demand and answers normally
## After updating
macOS may ask you to approve ChillMac's background helper. If fan control still does nothing after this update, open **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions** and make sure ChillMac is enabled under "Allow in the Background".
## If you've used ChillMac since its early releases
Very early versions installed the helper a different way, leaving files in `/Library`. That older copy still claims the same identifier, which blocks the new one from registering — so if fan control is still dead after updating and approving, remove the leftovers and restart ChillMac:
``` sudo launchctl bootout system/com.idevtim.ChillMac.Helper sudo rm -f /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.idevtim.ChillMac.Helper.plist sudo rm -f /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.idevtim.ChillMac.Helper ```
Most people won't need this. If ChillMac was installed recently, skip it.
